_comment: Written by the trading runs. impliedMove is a decimal or null. null means the straddle was not pulled - an open checklist item, not a placeholder to guess at. This file is a list of what is AHEAD: the pre-close run prunes catalysts once their date has passed and re-reads spot from a live quote, because a reference price carried from the day it was written makes every implied range wrong.
prunedNote: PRUNED BY THE 9/3 PRE-CLOSE. NOTHING WAS REMOVED AND THAT IS THE CORRECT OUTCOME: the file holds one row, ORCL 2026-09-10, whose date is still ahead. The AVGO row was already removed by this morning's open after its 9/2 print verified complete, so no catalyst in this file has a date that has passed. WHAT THIS PRUNE ACTUALLY CAUGHT IS THE SPOT, WHICH IS THE HALF OF THE STEP THAT IS EASY TO SKIP. The ORCL row carried spot 148.33, quoted at 13:49:50Z this morning. ORCL IS NOW 155.45 BID / 155.52 ASK at 2026-09-03T19:35:35.566768832Z, last 155.49, +6.655% on the bid against a 145.75 settled close, on a 0.07 spread that is 0.045% of mark. The carried figure was STALE BY 7.12, or 4.58% low. That is precisely the error this step exists to prevent - a reference price from the day it was written makes every implied range computed off it wrong, the way AMD sat on this board at 522.95 on a tape that traded 486 - and it is caught here before an implied move was ever computed against it rather than after. THE MOVE IS SECTOR-WIDE, NOT AN ORCL DISCLOSURE, AND IT MAKES BRANCH ONE BIND HARDER RATHER THAN SOFTER. SNOW reported after Wednesday's close with product revenue up 37% year over year and guided above consensus, and ran 21.9%; Waller signalled he could support holding rates in September; the enterprise-software complex re-rated together, NOW +6.0%, PLTR +8.3%, CRWD +4.5%, CRM +4.0%. So any enterprise-software entry considered between now and 9/10 would be reaching for an already-extended complex AND carrying a five-session time stop through the print - both halves of what branch one refuses, now true at once. ADBE IS RE-QUOTED ON THE SAME ROW AND MOVED THE OTHER WAY: 285.59 bid / 285.73 ask, +2.074% against a 279.79 close, LOWER than the 289.06 this row recorded this morning. It is named on this row rather than given its own because it shares one date and one branch, and it is updated here so the row does not refresh only the name that moved the way it expected. THE BRANCHES ARE DELIBERATELY NOT REWRITTEN. Both already carry a why, both were written five sessions early with nothing at stake, and rewriting a pre-commitment in the last half hour of a session because the tape moved is the exact behaviour this board refuses everywhere else - it is the moves-file version of reclassifying a fired invalidation. What a prune updates is the spot the branches are measured against, not the branches. IMPLIEDMOVE REMAINS NULL AND IS STILL NOT OWED. Item 3 binds before an earnings HOLD, not before a watch. The book is flat, nothing is carried overnight, and no position exists that could cross 9/10. A number this board did not pull does not exist, and a null here is an open checklist item rather than a placeholder to guess at. It becomes owed the moment a position exists that would cross the print. TONIGHT'S NINE-NAME CLUSTER - ZS, DOCU, LULU, PATH, IOT, ASAN, GWRE, AMBA and PL, all reporting after today's close - IS STILL NOT ADDED, and the 09:50 reasoning was re-checked rather than inherited: a row enters this file when a branch can be decided in advance for it, and with the book flat, no open specification and no candidate in that complex, nine rows would be noise wearing the shape of diligence. The rule that governs them at tomorrow's open is already written on this row's branch two - the reaction bar is not the entry, the day-2 or day-3 pullback that HOLDS its pre-print close is - and it is pre-registered in state.json entryWatch so tomorrow's open meets a written rule rather than an improvised one.

branches.cond: An entry considered in ORCL or ADBE themselves, or in an enterprise-software, database or cloud sympathy name, whose five-session time stop would carry it through 2026-09-10
branches.act: Refused unless the position is sized and stopped to survive the gap, or is closed before the print by a run that says so explicitly at entry
branches.why: The same arithmetic that refused AVGO on 9/2 and SMCI on 8/12, written forward to the date rather than rediscovered on the morning of 9/9. A -8% equity stop does not survive an event gap: the realistic bad case gaps THROUGH the exit rather than filling at it, so the stop is decorative and the real risk is the implied move, unpriced. The rulebook forbids holding an option through a print outright. The escape clause is named so it is a branch rather than a blanket ban - a position may be opened if it is deliberately closed before the print, and the run that opens it must write that intention down AT ENTRY rather than discover the conflict on 9/9. Note the concrete reach of this: an entry opened any day from 9/3 to 9/10 with a five-session stop lands on or after this date, so this branch binds essentially every enterprise-software entry available for the next week.

branches.cond: ORCL or ADBE gaps hard on 9/11 and the 9/11 open wants to trade the reaction
branches.act: Not on the reaction bar - the day-2 or day-3 pullback that HOLDS ITS PRE-PRINT CLOSE is the entry, and item 2 governs
branches.why: Written five sessions early because the version of this branch on the AVGO row was obeyed this morning and is the reason AVGO was refused at -5.68% rather than argued about. The record this board now has is unusually clean on the point: SAIC lost its 125.96 pre-print close on day 2 and was refused twice; NTNX the same; OLLI was PRE-REGISTERED on 9/2 as worth buying if it held, and on 9/3 it sat below both its 72.34 pre-print close and its own reaction-bar low and was refused; MDT held 1.53% above its line and is the one that was bought. The test is not whether the gap fades - MDT's faded hard - it is whether it holds the pre-print close. Nine names report tonight and more on 9/10, so this branch will be reached repeatedly.
